sections.heading: Voltage overshoot from voltage-loop bandwidth
sections.text: PFC overshoot on the bulk capacitor is a voltage-loop issue. The voltage-loop bandwidth must stay below 2*f_line (100 Hz for 50 Hz, 120 Hz for 60 Hz). If overshoot persists, add a notch filter at 2*f_line or reduce the voltage-loop bandwidth.

sections.heading: Slow settling by design
sections.text: PFC settling is dominated by the voltage-loop bandwidth, which is intentionally low (10-20 Hz) to avoid distorting the current reference. This is by design. If faster settling is required, consider adding a fast inner voltage loop or accepting the slow response.

sections.heading: 2*f_line ripple is inherent
sections.text: PFC output ripple at 2*f_line is inherent to single-phase PFC and cannot be eliminated by the controller. The ripple magnitude is: V_ripple = Pout/(2*pi*2*f_line*C_bulk). Reduce by increasing C_bulk. Controller gains cannot fix this.

sections.heading: Efficiency from plant losses
sections.text: PFC efficiency is dominated by the boost diode forward voltage and MOSFET switching/conduction losses. Consider totem-pole PFC with GaN/SiC for higher efficiency. The controller has limited ability to improve efficiency.

sections.heading: THD from current-loop issues
sections.text: If PFC fails across iterations, verify the current reference is tracking the rectified sine waveform. If THD is high, increase current-loop bandwidth. If PF is low despite low THD, check the current-loop phase shift at the line frequency.
